clue.text: Excellent line, offhand

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine remark delivered casually.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy manner is light and casual, treating something as unimportant, which is what offhand means.

clue.text: The Beatles record for example — it's white and wants finishing touches from George Martin

indicators.note: finishing touches come at the end, so the final letters of the two names are taken
wants means lacks, so the word is missing the named letters

blocks.note: albumen is egg white
the last letters of George and Martin

explanation.surface: The Beatles' White Album, needing producer George Martin's final polish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles is the official title of the double LP known as the White Album, which makes 'white' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles is an LP, a long-playing record, which is an example of an album.

clue.text: Dish initially soaked without restraint in port?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of soaked is used
in places the preceding letters inside the port

blocks.note: the first letter of soaked
OTT is over the top, unrestrained
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A meal drenched in port wine poured freely.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Value of hotel on either side of waterfront

blocks.note: the outer letters of waterfront are W and T, and 'either side' is read literally as the words W OR T
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An estate agent pricing a seafront hotel with water on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'either side' is spelt out as a phrase: one side or the other, so W, then the word OR, then T; 'on' places the hotel letter next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is a noun for the amount something is valued at, a straightforward synonym for value.

clue.text: Stunned — blooming keep course fencing green

indicators.note: a fence encloses ground, so the course surrounds the green

blocks.note: flowers that are blooming are out
a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort
to course is to hunt game with hounds
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: Golf-course instructions about a flourishing garden kept fenced in on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Course and green suggest golf; course is a verb for hunting and green means environmental.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer out for the count has been knocked down and cannot rise before the referee reaches ten, so he is stunned.

clue.text: See 4
Rod Stewart's opening band plays here

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Stewart is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Stewart
an orchestra plays in the pit below a stage

explanation.surface: A note about the venue where Rod Stewart's support act performs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Stewart looks like one name, but 'Rod' is the definition and Stewart only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the metal rod on which meat is turned for roasting over a fire.

clue.text: Belong in forward line without wingers following Guardiola's conclusion

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the last letter of the manager's name is taken
wingers play on the flanks, so dropping them leaves only the central letters

blocks.note: pert means forward or cheeky
the last letter of Guardiola
the middle two letters of line

explanation.surface: Pep Guardiola picking a forward line with no wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward, line and wingers all suggest football tactics; Pep Guardiola is the Manchester City manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to be connected or appropriate to something, which is to belong to it.

clue.text: Articulated lorry's shock absorber, say, and exhaust

indicators.note: articulated means spoken clearly, so the word is identified by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a tyre on a lorry wheel cushions the bumps, an example of a shock absorber

explanation.surface: Talking about a truck's suspension and its exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Articulated lorry is the British name for a semi-trailer truck, but the first word is split off as the signal; TYRE is the British spelling of tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To tire someone is to wear them out, which is what exhaust means as a verb.

clue.text: Doctor gets Ant & Dec on drug

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written; Ant & Dec are a British TV presenting duo

explanation.surface: A doctor recruits the TV presenters Ant and Dec, perhaps for a drug campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A decongestant is a medicine that clears a blocked nose, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Most crowded public transport, after Italy, is in France

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Observing that buses in France are fuller than those in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Busiest is the superlative of busy, which describes a place or vehicle packed with people.

clue.text: Space for each gold sovereign

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
per means for each, as in per person
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Allotting room per person and a gold coin, the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold sovereign' reads as a British coin, but the two words split: gold supplies letters and sovereign is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler, so he is a sovereign in the sense of monarch.

clue.text: Thoughtful sorts supply Polish shop stocking cane sugar at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letters of the two preceding words
a shop stocking goods holds them, so the letters are taken in
read as supple-y, in a supple or pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letters of cane and sugar

explanation.surface: Wise traders keep a Polish grocery stocked with cane sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply looks like the verb to provide, but it is read as the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophers are people given to deep reflection, so they are thoughtful types.

clue.text: Relating to climate change — melt glacier with what looks like 3 degrees, symbolically

indicators.note: a change alters the order of things, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the degree symbol is a small circle, so three of them look like three letter Os

explanation.surface: A warning that a three-degree rise in temperature will melt the glaciers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climate change' reads as one phrase, but it splits: climate ends the definition and change signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorological means concerning the weather and the atmosphere, the study of which underlies climate.

clue.text: Oven bake after removing lid

indicators.note: in a down clue the lid is the top, so the first letter is taken off

blocks.note: to roast is to bake in an oven

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a dish in the oven once the lid is off.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven.

clue.text: Feeder in love with a basket case husband

indicators.note: in puts one thing inside another, so love goes within the basket

blocks.note: a trug is a shallow wooden garden basket; 'case' casts it as the holder
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A lovelorn feeder obsessed with a husband who is a basket case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' looks like the idiom for a wreck of a person; here it is just the basket holding the love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is the long container animals feed from, a feeder in the farmyard sense.

clue.text: Pilot cuts Eton collars up

indicators.note: to collar is to seize and hold, so the words grip the answer within them
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of cuts and the start of Eton

explanation.surface: A pilot cutting the collars of Eton boys' uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the English public school famous for its stiff collars.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot a scheme is to try it out before launch, which is to test it.

clue.text: Problem after retirement home has very old woman collecting tax

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something in, so the woman holds the tax

blocks.note: at home means in
so means very, as in so good
old woman is slang for a mother, ma
NI is National Insurance, a UK payroll tax

explanation.surface: A pensioner's troubles after leaving work, with an old lady at home chasing taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, a trouble that comes once you have retired for the night.

clue.text: Dancer's colleague's drinking hot ground coffee before tango — shows start working

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the reindeer swallows the next word
ground coffee has been broken up, so the letters are crushed into a new order

blocks.note: Comet and Dancer are both among Santa's reindeer; the second 's is 'is'
in means fashionable, hot
taken as written, to be rearranged
T is tango in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer's partner gulps hot coffee before dancing the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer looks like a person on a dance floor, but it is one of Santa's reindeer, whose colleague is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or law that comes into effect begins to operate, so it starts working.

clue.text: Knocking back lager proved we must not appear to be too casual

indicators.note: knocking back a drink is downing it, but read literally it sends the word backwards
the named letters are told not to show up, so they are removed

blocks.note: pils is a pale lager
showed means proved or demonstrated
taken as written, the letters to drop

explanation.surface: Drinkers worried that downing lager will make them look too relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The W and E come out of the proved word, leaving SHOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod means careless and sloppy, the result of being too casual about one's work.

clue.text: Imprecise during old routine

blocks.note: in means during, as in in the night
ex means former, old
an act is a performer's routine

explanation.surface: Sloppy footwork during an outdated dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means not accurate or exact, a synonym for imprecise.

clue.text: Famous Austrian moving regularly from A to Z

indicators.note: moving letters about shifts their positions, so they are rearranged
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of from
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone well known from Austria who travels routinely from one place to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, the composer, was born in Salzburg and is the most famous Austrian of all.

clue.text: Examiner's German car parked on hill

blocks.note: Audi is a German car maker
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A driving examiner's German car left on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Examiner is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects accounts, so is an examiner of financial records.

clue.text: See 17
In toilet, abnormally wet forehead could be a warning sign?

indicators.note: abnormally means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order
in places the jumbled letters inside the toilet word

blocks.note: bog is British slang for a toilet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweaty brow in the lavatory as a hint that something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is one example of a warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware of the dog is the familiar notice on a gate, an example of a sign warning visitors.

clue.text: A corporation returning to support golf range

indicators.note: returning means going back, so these words are read backwards

blocks.note: G is golf in the phonetic alphabet
taken as written
a corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A company coming back to sponsor a golf driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts the reversed letters under G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the complete range of something, from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Employed American journalist

blocks.note: US for United States
ed is editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A US reporter with a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Used is the past tense of use, so employed in the sense of put to use.

clue.text: Simple craft's blocking bridge

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so craft goes within bridge

blocks.note: art is craft or skill; the 's is 'is'
a span is a bridge or the stretch it covers

explanation.surface: A plain boat stuck under a bridge, holding up traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and plain, after the frugal ancient Spartans, so a close synonym for simple.

clue.text: Ultimately Victor Mature's struggling to accept mistake in script?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of Victor is used
struggling suggests twisting and writhing, so the letters are thrown into a new order
accepting something means taking it in, so the single letter goes inside the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written; the 's is 'is'
the last letter of Victor

explanation.surface: The Hollywood actor Victor Mature having trouble taking a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Mature reads as the film star's name, but the two words are split: one gives a letter, the other is the jumbled fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printed or written text, so a mistake in a script fits.

clue.text: To a Morse aficionado, Endeavour's first episode's ending appears to be weakly affectionate

indicators.note: someone fluent in Morse code hears a letter as its pattern of dots and dashes
the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Endeavour is E, which in Morse code is a single dot
the last letter of episode

explanation.surface: A fan of Inspector Morse finds the first episode of the prequel Endeavour sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour is the TV prequel to Inspector Morse, which makes 'Morse' look like the detective; it is the telegraph code.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote is to be foolishly or excessively fond of someone, a weak, soft-headed kind of affection.

clue.text: Bug essentially caught in insect trap

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is taken
something caught in another thing is held inside it

blocks.note: the middle letter of bug
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug stuck in an insect trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect trap' reads as one device; trap is the definition, in its slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Bother doctor with a temperature

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Troubling a doctor about having a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Bother looks like a verb but is the mild exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild oaths uttered in irritation, so the interjections are synonyms.
